title: Inquest slams RCMP 'understaffing, underfunding' on reserves
article: There's "an alarming trend" toward understaffing and underfunding RCMP detachments on northern Manitoba First Nations,saysan inquest into the death of a man being held on one by police.

The commentcame ina report bya provincial court judge conducting aninquest into the case of Dennis St. Paul, who died in Norway House in January 2005 after fighting with an RCMP officer who was trying to arrest him for parole violations.
In the inquest's report, released Wednesday, Judge Brent Stewart described an "alarming trend" toward understaffing and underfunding in the RCMP in many northern native communities.
At the time of the shooting, the Norway House RCMP detachment had nine staff members posted for a community of approximately 7,000 people.

Stewart described the situation as being "grossly understaffed," noting that RCMP's own models for calculating police-to-citizen ratios indicate the detachment should have had at least 19 officers based on population and number of charges processed.
"Norway House citizens are at greater risk of having less effective law enforcement and personal safety due to the understaffing of the RCMP detachments," Stewart wrote.

"In addition, RCMP members are not only subject to burnout due to the number of files to which they have responsibility at any one time but more importantly, they risk personal safety and ultimately life due to such circumstances."

Stewart recommended the Mounties meet first with the province and then with the federal government to ask for more money to fund an increase in resources in Norway House and other northern communities.

St. Paul was released from jail six months before the shooting after serving a 4 1/2-year sentence fora series of break-ins.Police had issued a warrant for his arrest, saying he violatedthe conditions of his release and failed to report to a parole office.
Const. Darcy Muth, who was making the arrest, thought at first that St. Paul was going to co-operate, so he decided not to handcuff him.
But as they walked out of the restaurant where the arrest took place and approached a police vehicle, St. Paul bolted, according to the inquest report.
After a chase,St. Paul andMuth scuffled for the officer's baton.The inquest report said St. Paul got the upper hand and struckMuthtwice on the head.
Fearing for his life, Muth shot St. Paul twice - including at least one shot to the chest,the inquest report said.St. Paul died shortly afterward.
In the days following the death of St. Paul, who was a native man, some community leaders said the reserve's sour relationship with the RCMP had contributed to the shooting.

But the judge noted that both Muth and a second officer who was involved in the chase were also aboriginal people.The judge wrote that this should "instill more confidence" in the police service in these communities.
In his report, Stewart said it was "unfortunate" that "some leaders in the provincial aboriginal community" made the issue a political one.
Their actions "indirectly [affected] the community's perception of the police investigation and ultimately this inquest," Stewart said.
